result:
The full test suite (all existing tests plus the three new ones) passes with no output/errors.

**Summary:**
- `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVParserAgentTest.java` — 34 tests covering `parse()` overloads (String/Reader/File/Path), `Builder`, header map/names, duplicate/missing header validation, comments, record numbers, line numbers, EOL detection, close/iterator/stream semantics, null handling, trailing delimiters, `maxRows`, and deprecated constructors.
- `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/csv/LexerAgentTest.java` — 33 tests covering `nextToken()` across tokens/records/EOF/comments/quoting/escaping, error conditions (unclosed quotes, invalid trailing data), position/line tracking, `isDelimiter`/`isEscape`/`isQuoteChar`/`isCommentStart`/`isEndOfFile`/`isStartOfLine`, `readEscape()`, `trimTrailingSpaces()`, and empty-line handling.
- `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/csv/TokenAgentTest.java` — 10 tests covering initial state, `reset()`, content accumulation, `toString()` formatting (including null type), and the `Type` enum.

All three are self-contained (no shared helpers/inheritance) and match the existing JUnit 5 (Jupiter) style used elsewhere in the project. Verified with `mvn test -Dtest=CSVParserAgentTest,LexerAgentTest,TokenAgentTest` → 77/77 passing, and a full `mvn test` run confirms no regressions.
